spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The mathematical work is a fiber count. A fixed ℓ-swap can be encoded by many ordered block decompositions: once one swapped element is marked in each block, every one of the k−ℓ unmarked elements independently chooses one of ℓ blocks on each of the A and B sides, while permutations of the marked elements supply the two factorial factors.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: For a fixed swap of ℓ-element subsets, the source counts decompositions A=A₁∪⋯∪Aℓ with αⱼ∈Aⱼ and analogously for B. The remaining k−ℓ elements have ℓ choices each, giving ℓ^(k−ℓ) decompositions on each side; including the orderings gives multiplicity (ℓ!)²ℓ^(2(k−ℓ)).
directed.conceptual_reading: The passage isolates overcounting as a constant-fiber phenomenon: block decompositions are redundant presentations of the same swap. Marking one swapped element per block simultaneously enforces nonemptiness and separates forced structure from independent assignments of unused elements.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge is the forgetful map from a labeled pair of block decompositions with marked representatives to the underlying pair of swapped ℓ-subsets. Its stated constant fiber size supplies the normalization needed when summing over decompositions.
directed.boundary_or_failure: This establishes only the multiplicity internal to the chosen decomposition scheme, under equal cardinality k and one marked swapped element per block. It does not validate the analytic swap terms or any conjectural correlation estimate to which the weight is later applied.
directed.uncertainty: The extracted exponents and squared factorial are typographically degraded, but the prose and assigned metadata consistently support the reading (ℓ!)²ℓ^(2(k−ℓ)).

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The same underlying pair (m,n) survives a large change of presentation. Expanding the shifted divisor sums into μ- and ν-factors, choosing distinguished factors, distributing the remaining factors among ℓ slots, and absorbing them into a rescaled (∗)-system creates many equation systems without changing m or n; counting this fiber recovers exactly the swap multiplicity.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source expands τ_A(m) and τ_B(n) through factorizations m=μ₁⋯μ_k and n=ν₁⋯ν_k, partitions the indices into ℓ blocks, and starts from equations Nⱼmⱼ=Mⱼnⱼ+hⱼ with ∏Mⱼ=∏Nⱼ. After selecting divisors μⱼ,νⱼ and writing complementary factors with hats, it rescales each equation to a new tilde system representing the same m,n. Assigning each of the k−ℓ unused μ-factors and ν-factors to one of ℓ slots gives ℓ^(k−ℓ) choices per side, and ordering the ℓ distinguished factors gives (ℓ!)², hence (ℓ!)²ℓ^(2(k−ℓ)).
directed.conceptual_reading: This is an invariance-under-refactorization argument. The equation system remembers how prime/divisor factors were routed through slots, whereas the original summand remembers only their total products m and n. Forgetting that routing exposes a redundant fiber whose size can be divided out.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge objects are the divisor-factor expansion, the index-block partition, and the rescaled tilde (∗)-system. They translate between a global summand indexed by (m,n) and local direction-discrepancy equations; the global product balance for the tilde coefficients preserves membership in the same class of systems.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The count is asserted to remain valid whether some hⱼ vanish, and common factors in a tilde coefficient pair may be divided from the equation. This is multiplicity bookkeeping, not a proof of the conjectural shifted-divisor evaluation or of the correctness of every resulting analytic term.
directed.uncertainty: OCR substantially confuses hats, stars, products, and exponents in the displayed formulas. The factor-allocation construction and final multiplicity are recoverable from the surrounding prose, but finer identities involving individual decorated variables should not be reconstructed from this span.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The conclusion organizes the comparison by discrepancy strata: the number of nonzero hⱼ determines the swap order seen on the recipe side. Thus one convolutional delta-method representation does not match a single recipe term; after all zero/nonzero strata, all nonempty block partitions, and the common multiplicity correction are assembled, it matches the surviving family of swap terms.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Choose ℓ by T^ℓ≤X<T^(ℓ+1), partition A and B into ℓ nonempty subsets, and evaluate a convolution of ℓ shifted divisor sums subject to mⱼNⱼ−nⱼMⱼ=hⱼ. The source says that all hⱼ nonzero produce ℓ-swap terms, while exactly ℓ′ nonzero discrepancies produce ℓ′-swap terms. Summing over all partitions and accounting for multiplicities yields agreement with the CFKRS-recipe evaluation.
directed.conceptual_reading: The zero pattern of the discrepancy vector is a stratifying invariant that compresses many local equation systems into swap order. Lower swap orders are not exceptions to the ℓ-block construction; they arise as boundary strata where some discrepancies vanish.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge connects delta-method convolutions of partitioned shifted divisor sums to the recipe's swap expansion. Rigorous Euler-product identifications support the termwise arithmetic bridge for some terms, while the zero/nonzero h-pattern selects which swap stratum a contribution represents.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The delta-method evaluation is explicitly conjectural, so the final equality is conditional even though the cited identification of two Euler products is rigorous. The span claims agreement with recipe terms, not an independent proof of the moment conjecture; extension to other L-function families is only proposed as future research.
directed.uncertainty: The displayed convolution and the symbol for nonzero are mildly degraded by extraction, but the prose clearly states the stratum correspondence and distinguishes the rigorous Euler-product step from the conjectural average.
